Run from the repo root: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree` and `subject` to YOUR checkout (both absolute). Two dedup sites were measured per integration-test-revert-verify §A33: the name-keyed Map (M1) and the used-marker loop (M2/M3) — a one-site fix produces a DUPLICATE instead of a fix, so both are mutated separately. This spec pins the merged LIST; the product effect lives in the companion spec `inheritance-merge-a2c868e9.effect.spec.json`. Every `expect` is the MEASURED red set (§A97); the prediction is quoted in each `_note`. ⛔ `red_re` anchors on the `● <suite> › <title>` failure header, NOT on the bare `[Xn]` key: jest echoes the SOURCE LINE of a neighbouring `it(...)` in the diff context, so a key-only pattern would report a green axis as red (§A44 — the citation is not a verdict).

M1_grounding_map_last_wins._note: Rebuilds the grounding map LAST-WINS (the pre-fix shape), type-preserving: the map stays Map<string, Rule[]>, each name just keeps a single-element bucket. This is defect D1 — a grounding's earlier conditional rule is dropped before any logic runs. Predicted: U1 on the unit harness, G1+G2 on the effect harness.

M2_splice_guard_removed._note: Drops the once-only guard around the splice, so the grounding rules are re-emitted for EVERY universal rule they shadow. This is defect D2. It has NO product effect: applyInheritanceRuleStep opens with `if (properties[rule.targetPropertyName] !== undefined) continue`, so the duplicate is swallowed and the write is idempotent — the effect harness is expected to stay GREEN, and that is the measurement proving the guard's product-level inertness, not a gap in the axis.

M3_used_marker_removed._note: Removes the used-marker, so the SECOND loop appends every grounding rule a second time. Same idempotence argument as M2 for the product effect; the list is visibly wrong.
